entries.title: Luke 23:1
segments: 1-5. Christ brought before Pilate.

entries.title: Luke 23:2
segments: Perverting the nation; exciting the people to rebel against the Roman government. Give tribute; pay taxes. The accusation which the Jews brought against Jesus before Pilate was not that of blasphemy in claiming to be the Son of God, for which their council had condemned him.

; it was that of treason against the Roman government. His claiming to be the Son of God was no crime in a Roman court. They could not induce Pilate for this to put him to death. They therefore invented another accusation, and sought false witnesses to support it. So that while they condemned him for what was no crime, they sought to have Pilate condemn him for a crime which he never committed. Justly did he who knew what was in them, say, "Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?

entries.title: Luke 23:3
segments: Thou sayest it; Jesus not only acknowledged himself to be the King of the Jews, but explained to Pilate that his kingdom was not of this world; so that he found no fault in him on this ground.

entries.title: Luke 23:5
segments: He stirreth up the people; causing tumults among them. All Jewry; the whole Jewish country.

entries.title: Luke 23:7
segments: He sent him to Herod; seeking thus to get rid of the case altogether. This was Herod Antipas, who put John to death. He was son to Herod the Great, under whose reign Christ was born,
; uncle to Herod Agrippa, by whom James was killed, and who was eaten of worms,
; and great-uncle to that Agrippa who was almost persuaded by Paul to become a Christian.

entries.title: Luke 23:9
segments: He answered him nothing; the Saviour would not answer questions prompted by a vain curiosity, without any desire to know the truth.

entries.title: Luke 23:11
segments: Men of war; the soldiers of his guard. Set him at naught; treated him with contempt.

entries.title: Luke 23:15
segments: Is done unto him; rather, is done by him. The two examinations before Pilate and Herod had brought to light no action of Jesus worthy of death.

entries.title: Luke 23:16
segments: Chastise; scourge or whip him.

entries.title: Luke 23:17
segments: Of necessity; it was the custom, and the people would be displeased if he should not comply with it.
. This shows the manner in which the word necessity is sometimes used in the Bible.

entries.title: Luke 23:18
segments: 18-25. Christ condemned by Pilate.

entries.title: Luke 23:22
segments: As civil government is an ordinance of God, established for the protection of the innocent, and the condemnation and punishment of the guilty, magistrates who, against evidence, acquit the guilty and condemn the innocent, are an abomination to the Lord. Injustice under the cover of law is aggravated wickedness. False witnesses and corrupt judges merit, and without repentance will receive a most awful condemnation.

entries.title: Luke 23:26
segments: Simon, a Cyrenian;

entries.title: Luke 23:28
segments: Weep for yourselves, and for your children; on account of the great calamities that were coming upon them.

entries.title: Luke 23:29
segments: Blessed are the barren; it were better not to have children than to have them exposed to such distresses.

entries.title: Luke 23:30
segments: To the mountains, Fall on us; to shelter us from the wrath of God. Compare
. They feel that it is better to be crushed beneath the weight of the mountains, than to meet God in judgment, and bear the fierceness of his wrath.

entries.title: Luke 23:31
segments: If they do these things in a green tree; this was a proverb. A green tree represented one innocent and good; a dry tree, those who were wicked. If such distress as that of crucifixion would come upon one who was perfectly innocent, what would be the distress which, under the just indignation of God, would come upon those who were so exceedingly wicked as to murder his beloved Son?

entries.title: Luke 23:32
segments: Malefactors; evil-doers, thieves, robbers, etc.

entries.title: Luke 23:33
segments: 33-49. The crucifixion.

entries.title: Luke 23:34
segments: Father, forgive them; this was a prayer for the pardon of his murderers. Jesus Christ, who was most compassionate and benevolent in his life, was also most kind and forgiving in his death. He desired the everlasting salvation even of his murderers, and for it he was willing to give up his life.

entries.title: Luke 23:39
segments: One of the malefactors; Matthew and Mark speak as if both the robbers had at first reviled him. One however repented, rebuked his companion, confessed the justice of their punishment, and looked to Christ for salvation.

entries.title: Luke 23:40
segments: True repentance leads a sinner to feel and acknowledge the justice of his condemnation, and at the same time to look to Jesus for salvation; expecting through him to receive it, that when absent from the body he may be present with the Lord.

entries.title: Luke 23:42
segments: When thou comest into thy kingdom; more literally, When thou comest in the kingdom; that is, when thou comest in glory as the King Messiah. This will be when he shall "appear the second time without sin unto salvation" for all who have believed in him.

entries.title: Luke 23:43
segments: Paradise; the place and state of blessedness.

entries.title: Luke 23:50
segments: A counsellor; a member of the great Jewish council. 50-56. Christ's burial.

entries.title: Luke 23:51
segments: Deed of them; the doings of the council in condemning Christ. Waited for the kingdom of God; the reign of Jesus as the Messiah.

entries.title: Luke 23:54
segments: That day was the preparation; the preparation for the solemnities of the next day, which was the Sabbath.
